topic: Rex Reklaitis: Operations Research and Process Systems Engineering
title: Rex Reklaitis: Operations Research and Process Systems Engineering
session_title: In Honor of Professor Rex Reklaitis' 80th Birthday (Invited Talks)
abstract: In this presentation we highlight the pioneering contributions of Prof. Rex Reklaitis in the area of Operations Research, which has become a major science base for Process Systems Engineering (PSE). We first give a general overview of the educational and research contributions by Prof. Reklaitis, as well as his strong leadership at the professional level. We then focus on his contributions in the areas of geometric programming, flexibility, batch design and scheduling, process operations, optimization of supply chains, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and optimization under uncertainty. It is clear that Prof. Rex Reklaitis has become a unique pioneer and leader who has been able to introduce Operations Research in Process Systems Engineering, and make it thrive into new directions in order to broaden the scope of PSE.

topic: You Want to Do What? Rex’s Brainchild: The New Directions Committee (1996 – 2006)
title: You Want to Do What? Rex’s Brainchild: The New Directions Committee (1996 – 2006)
session_title: In Honor of Professor Rex Reklaitis' 80th Birthday (Invited Talks)
abstract: Although not the first advisory council ever developed, Professor Rex Reklaitis had a vision: Grow and expand Purdue’s Chemical Engineering Department using its Industrial Advisory Council, called the “New Directions Committee.” This group of individuals was the first alumni group at Purdue that took up the task of raising 100% private funds in order to build an addition on the existing Chemical Engineering Building. Ms. Grubbe, a member of the group for 10 years, will discuss Professor Reklaitis’ huge contribution to Purdue and how he went about it.

topic: Honoring Prof. Reklaitis' Contributions to Mentoring and Energy and Sustainability Research
title: Honoring Prof. Reklaitis' Contributions to Mentoring and Energy and Sustainability Research
session_title: In Honor of Professor Rex Reklaitis' 80th Birthday (Invited Talks)
abstract: The process systems engineering tools Prof. Reklaitis and his collaborators have developed over the past five decades have been utilized in a wide range of application areas, and have found a home over the past decade in applications to energy and sustainability. This presentation will highlight the contributions to various energy fields and in the light of the global need for sustainable energy and chemical production. In addition, this presentation will offer some highlights from his mentoring of young and experienced researchers during his 50+ years at Purdue University.

topic: Some Thoughts on the Future of Advanced Drug Delivery Systems: New Materials and Models
title: Some Thoughts on the Future of Advanced Drug Delivery Systems: New Materials and Models
session_title: In Honor of Professor Rex Reklaitis' 80th Birthday (Invited Talks)
abstract: Engineering the molecular design of intelligent biomaterials by controlling structure, recognition and specificity is the first step in coordinating and duplicating complex biological and physiological processes. Recent developments in siRNA and protein delivery have been directed towards the preparation of targeted formulations for protein delivery to specific sites, use of environmentally-responsive polymers to achieve pH- or temperature-triggered delivery, usually in modulated mode, and improvement of the behavior of their mucoadhesive behavior and cell recognition. We address design and synthesis characteristics of novel crosslinked networks capable of protein release as well as artificial molecular structures capable of specific molecular recognition of biological molecules. Molecular imprinting and microimprinting techniques, which create stereo-specific three-dimensional binding cavities based on a biological compound of interest, can lead to preparation of biomimetic materials for intelligent drug delivery, drug targeting, and tissue engineering. We have been successful in synthesizing novel glucose- and protein-binding molecules based on non-covalent directed interactions formed via molecular imprinting techniques within aqueous media. We have also developed structurally superior materials to serve as effective carriers for siRNA delivery to combat Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.

topic: Navigating Scheduling Research through Professor Reklaitis’ Career & Contributions
title: Navigating Scheduling Research through Professor Reklaitis’ Career & Contributions
session_title: In Honor of Professor Rex Reklaitis' 80th Birthday (Invited Talks)
abstract: Over his career spanning over five decades, Professor G.V. Reklaitis has been a visionary and pioneer in the general area of batch and continuous scheduling and operation of chemical, pharmaceutical, energy and manufacturing processes, and their wider enterprise and supply chain networks. In this presentation, we will provide an overview of his many contributions in this field from a historical perspective, and highlight the major impact that these developments have had in the evolution of the field of process systems engineering.
